shots.title: Inspect block/buzz shared event log, agent pool, orchestration benchmark, and open collaboration gaps
shots.notes: Inspected Buzz at commit 87b3fcd3c0131683569dd4268b099d18b25dcd5e and recorded the transferable event-log, identity, concurrency, callback, verification, status, and evaluation patterns plus the transport, crypto, and chat-first boundaries SLOPE should not copy.

shots.title: Select the canonical SLOPE Team Round with one team outcome and actor-attributed shots

hazards.description: The first Team Round pass selected the right container but under-specified ledger authority, identity trust, lease fencing, access enforcement, statistical estimands, and benchmark reproducibility. Three independent review lanes requested changes, which were resolved before approval.

shots.notes: Selected one Team Round with one canonical score-versus-par outcome and actor-attributed evidence. Coordination overhead remains separate; actor and role handicaps are risk-adjusted descriptive estimates rather than causal rankings; single-player scorecards remain one-actor Team Rounds.

shots.title: Map identity, leases, callbacks, verification, learning, status, and evaluation into downstream sprints
shots.notes: Expanded S264-S264.2 into domain/scoring, integrity/security, and workflow/evaluation contracts; kept S265-S267 as the canonical sprint-id migration; added S268-S272 for ledger access control, fenced leases and typed resources, attribution and learning, multiplayer workflow and status, and reproducible evaluation.

shots.title: Compile and validate roadmap sources, projection, map, and focused sprint contexts
shots.notes: Compiled the compatibility projection and passed roadmap validate-sources, roadmap compile --check, map --check, focused contexts for S260.1/S264.1/S268/S272, and git diff --check. Independent architecture, security, and data/scoring re-reviews approved with no remaining blockers.

conditions.description: The source project is a collaboration system with transport, identity, and chat assumptions that do not directly fit SLOPE's repository-native enforcement model.
Issue #669 spans product metaphor, store authority, concurrency control, access boundaries, scoring methodology, operator surfaces, and evaluation reproducibility.

special_plays: Used three independent review lanes and completed a changes-requested re-review loop before marking the roadmap sprint complete.
Split every new design and implementation sprint to four tickets, eliminating the validator's new ticket-count warnings.

training.description: Renewable leases without epochs and fencing still permit stale writers after reassignment.
training.outcome: S264.1 and S269 now require authoritative time, monotonic lease epochs, fencing tokens on protected writes, and stale-token rejection.

training.description: Actor labels and session separation are not sufficient trust anchors for access control or independent verification.
training.outcome: The roadmap binds actors and sessions to authenticated principals and defines verifier conflicts across authors, contributors, delegators, aliases, and sessions.

training.description: Actor and role performance from non-random assignments cannot be treated as causal or inherently comparable.
training.outcome: S264 and S270 define risk-adjusted descriptive estimands with exposure, difficulty, sample minimums, missingness, reliability, and uncertainty.

nutrition.description: roadmap validate-sources and roadmap compile --check passed with no new ticket-count warnings; remaining warnings are historical.
map --check and git diff --check passed; focused contexts for S260.1, S264.1, S268, and S272 showed the intended dependency and evidence chain.
Independent architecture, security/risk, and data/scoring reviewers approved the review-fix commit with zero remaining blocking findings.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: The Buzz comparison was useful once it stopped being a feature checklist and became a set of contracts SLOPE can enforce in its own domain.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: Start S261 with the shared common-dir store recovery. Do not begin the Team Round schema before S264-S264.2 formalize the contracts and S267 lands canonical sprint identity.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: The reviewers converged on the same hidden fault line: identity, visibility, and lease expiry are harmless labels until the store makes them enforceable.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: SLOPE now has a credible path from today's worktree claims to measurable, recoverable multiplayer rounds without weakening repository-native discipline.

bunker_locations: A renewable lease without a monotonic epoch and fencing token permits stale writes after reassignment.
A second coordination ledger beside the existing event store creates competing sources of truth and non-deterministic projections.
Actor or role labels cannot establish verifier independence; trust must resolve to an authenticated principal.
Actor and role handicaps from selected assignments are descriptive estimates, not causal rankings.
yardage_book_updates: docs/research/buzz-multiplayer-collaboration.md records the Team Round decision, trust and integrity boundaries, scoring semantics, evaluation contract, and roadmap mapping.
Phase 62 now contains S264-S264.2 as separate domain/scoring, integrity/security, and workflow/evaluation contracts.
Phase 64 now contains S268-S272 with four tickets each for ledger access, fenced resources, attribution, workflow/status, and evaluation.
course_management_notes: S261 remains the immediate next sprint because one common-dir store is the substrate every later coordination contract assumes.
S265 depends on S264.2, and S268 depends on both S264.2 and the S267 canonical sprint-id release.
